biography: Born in Uddingston, Scotland, Paul di Resta’s journey into motorsports wasn’t paved with silver spoons, but fueled by sheer grit and a deep-seated passion for speed. Unlike many of his peers who started in karting at a young age, Paul's entry was delayed, forced to work part-time jobs to fund his initial forays into amateur racing series. He caught the eye of a local racing team owner after a particularly daring maneuver at Knockhill, a move where he threaded his way through a gap most wouldn't attempt, showcasing a raw talent that couldn't be ignored. This led to his first real seat in a junior formula series. While his early career was marked by flashes of brilliance, financial constraints always loomed, forcing him to fight harder for every opportunity. Now, at 23, he's a rising star in the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship, piloting the #22 Oreca 07 for a prominent team. Though still relatively new to the world of endurance racing, he is determined to prove his mettle against seasoned veterans.
drivingStyle: Di Resta's driving style can best be described as calculated aggression. He's not one for flamboyant oversteer or late-braking heroics, but rather a master of precision and consistency. He meticulously studies track data, focusing on optimizing every corner exit for maximum speed. His defensive style often frustrates competitors, as he is adept at positioning his car to make overtaking extremely difficult, even if it means sacrificing a bit of his own momentum. He is known for his exceptional tire management skills, coaxing every last bit of performance from his rubber, especially in long stints.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of driving gloves, a gift from his grandfather.
Listens to classical music to calm his nerves before a race.
Insists on personally inspecting every tire before it's mounted on his car.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about speed; it's about calculated control. It's about knowing when to push and when to defend, and having the courage to do both."
careerHighlight: Winning the Scottish Formula Ford Championship in 2021 after a season-long battle, proving his ability to perform under pressure and overcome financial disadvantages.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2023 Le Mans Prototype Challenge race, a mistake caused by a momentary lapse in concentration after a grueling stint.
